reason: PO lists 'compound corymb' as a synonym of corymb inflorescence (PO_0030124), so mapping it to corymb present follows PO itself. The 'compound' detail is something PO also leaves out.

A tendril at the tip of the rachis (PO_0025366) exists only on compound leaves, as in Vicia and Lathyrus. On a simple leaf such as Gloriosa or Flagellaria, the tendril is a leaf apex tendril (PO_0025363), so a bare 'leaf' bearer is ambiguous.

FLOPO unequal is defined for like parts within one set that differ in size. 'Variable-sized' in a taxon description often means variation between plants or specimens, which is a different character. The word is ambiguous between the two readings.

On a trunk, having no flared base means having no buttresses, so 'not buttressed' (negation of FLOPO_0991138, as in the unbuttressed rule R0269) is safe. On corolla tubes, petioles and similar parts, 'flared base' has nothing to do with buttresses.

The surface is still papillose (FLOPO_0991059), so the mapping is true even though 'glandular' is not carried. This follows R0355, where 'glandular puberulent' kept the main hair-cover term. The glandular detail can be added as a second annotation (PATO_0002117).

A pleasant odour fits sweet-scented, whose definition says 'sweet, pleasant odour' and which has 'fragrant' as a related synonym. 'Perfumed' was accepted the same way (R1725). The 'flower' bearer does not limit the word to scent, so it is removed.

PATO tessellated (PATO_0104307) means structural elements in four-sided units that give a chequered look. Its source is the NSW flora glossary, where it is the term for bark cracked into squarish blocks. That matches 'blocky bark', but on other parts 'blocky' is a vague shape word.
This follows R0911, where 'moundlike' plants and stigmas map to domed. Pulvinate means cushion-shaped and would be a narrower claim.

The wrinkling is in the veins or network, not on the whole surface, so plain rugose puts it on the wrong part. No existing class says 'rugose venation' as a single value. It needs the part-of-bearer pattern rather than a word rule.
Setaceous-tipped means ending in a bristle. This matches R0128 'bristle-tipped' and the aristate rule C207, both mapped to awn present, and PO awn (PO_0025349) has bristle and seta as synonyms.
Glands set in small pits mark the surface with dots that are glands, which is the definition of FLOPO gland-dotted (FLOPO_0991174). The pits are how the gland sits, not a separate surface sculpture.
Narrow lines of a different colour are FLOPO streaked (FLOPO_0991206). As with 'brown-mottled' (R2002) and 'dark-mottled' (R1300), the pattern term is mapped and the colour is a separate annotation.

In the examples, the veins are quilted-sunken above, so the veins lie below the blade surface. This is the same reading as impressed, etched, recessed and engraved, all mapped to sunken (PATO_0002416). The quilted look belongs to the blade between the veins, which is bullate (FLOPO_0991122).
'X surrounded by hairs' describes hairs on another structure placed around X. That is a relation between two parts (pattern 09), and saying 'trichome present' of X puts the hairs on the wrong bearer.
This follows R0025, where 'glomerulate' (in dense clusters) maps to aggregated, which has 'clustered' as a synonym. Condensed means thickened or pressed tightly together, which is a different idea.

If all members have the same form, they are not in two distinct forms. So 'not dimorphic' (negation of FLOPO_0991092) follows from the word, even if it says less than the word does. This mirrors R0086 'homostylous' mapped to not heterostylous.
'Weakly marked' means faint or not clearly visible. This is the reading of R0776 'weakly defined' and the 'obscure' and 'indistinct' rules, all mapped to inconspicuous with no part limit.
'Striped' is an exact synonym of PATO banded (PATO_0001946). Under the colour-pattern precedent (R2002 brown-mottled), the pattern is mapped and brown is annotated separately.

Venation without loops, such as craspedodromous or parallel, is indeed not brochidodromous (secondaries joined in arches), so the negation holds. The first check had the logic backwards. Outside venation, for hairs or tendrils, 'looped' means something else.

A pseudopedicellate flower or spikelet is still borne on a stalk. FLOPO stipitate is defined loosely as borne on a stalk or stipe, without saying what the stalk is made of. This mirrors the pseudo- rules R0387 and R0638, which map to the look-alike value.

This follows R0564 'darker brown' mapped to brown and R0568 'darker yellow' mapped to yellow. The hue is stated, and the comparison is dropped because the other part is not given. It is not an absolute dark orange.
Flecks are small spots of another colour, so spotted (PATO_0000333) is the pattern. Brown is annotated separately, as in R2002 brown-mottled.
Cirrate means ending in a cirrus, a tendril-like coiling tip. This follows R0651 'cirrose' and R1034 'cirriform', both mapped to tendrilous. Curled is wrong.

For a whole plant or its stems, free-standing means self-supporting, which is not climbing (negation of FLOPO_0991108, as in R1610 'non-climbing'). For other parts, 'free' means not fused, which is a different character.
Glanduliform means gland-like. PATO glandular is defined as having the look of a gland, which is exactly R0179 'gland-like' mapped to glandular.
'Non-flowering' describes shoots, culms or plants that bear no flowers, so 'flower absent' fits only those bearers.

Perennating describes organs (buds, rhizomes, bulbs, corms) that carry the plant through the bad season. The organ itself need not live more than two years, so 'perennial life span' does not fit those bearers. No existing class covers this survival role.
This follows R1018, where 'satiny' (a soft sheen) maps to glistening and 'lustrous' was handled the same way. Sericeous (silky) means a cover of silky hairs and is not meant here.

PATO translucent is defined as low opacity, which covers partial translucence. Prefixed degree words keep the base term, as in semiamplexicaul mapped to clasping and subimpressed mapped to sunken plus the qualifier 'sub'.

The word is ambiguous. It can mean two or more parts of the same width (an equal-size reading, which FLOPO_0991102 covers only for overall size), the same width throughout (parallel-sided), or 'as wide as long'. No single class fits all three.
